plugin.kmac.title: KMAC (SP 800-185)
plugin.kmac.param.algorithmHint: KMAC128 and KMAC256 run on cSHAKE128 and cSHAKE256. The XOF variants KMACXOF128/256 do not fix the output length in advance.
plugin.kmac.param.keyHint: 0 to 64 bytes as hex digits. KMAC encodes the key together with its length, so any length works. Never type a real key here.
plugin.kmac.param.inputHint: 0 to 200 bytes. The message may be empty.
plugin.kmac.param.customizationHint: Any text that separates this use of KMAC from others, e.g. “My Tagged Application”. Up to 64 bytes of UTF-8 text; it may be empty.
plugin.kmac.param.outputLengthHint: How many bytes KMAC outputs. KMAC puts L into its input, so a shorter tag is not the start of a longer one; KMACXOF does not. 168 bytes are one KMAC128 rate block.
plugin.kmac.param.encodingHint: Text is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Hex lets you enter any bytes, two hex digits per byte.
plugin.kmac.param.detailHint: “Per step mapping” shows θ, ρ, π, χ and ι of each of the 24 rounds. “Per round” runs one round per step, “Per permutation” all 24 rounds in one step.
plugin.kmac.op.encodeKey: Encode the key into whole rate blocks
plugin.kmac.op.pad: Pad the input to whole rate blocks
plugin.kmac.op.absorb: Absorb a block into the rate
plugin.kmac.op.squeeze: Squeeze output bytes from the rate
plugin.kmac.sponge.label: Keccak-f[1600]
plugin.kmac.step.initial: {{algorithm}} is a MAC built on {{cshake}} (SP 800-185 §4): from the {{keyBytes}}-byte key K and the {{bytes}}-byte message X it computes a {{outputBytes}}-byte tag. cSHAKE gets the function name N = “KMAC”, the customization string S and the input bytepad(encode_string(K), r) ‖ X ‖ right_encode(L). The state A has 1600 bits (25 lanes of 64 bits) and starts as all zeros; the rate r = {{rateBits}} bits ({{rateLanes}} lanes) takes the input, the capacity c = {{capacityBits}} bits stays hidden. This lab is a teaching tool: never type a real key into it.
plugin.kmac.step.initialXof: {{algorithm}} is the XOF variant of KMAC (SP 800-185 §4.3.1): KMAC on {{cshake}}, but the input ends with right_encode(0) instead of the output length, so it can output as many bytes as you want. Here it turns the {{keyBytes}}-byte key K and the {{bytes}}-byte message X into {{outputBytes}} bytes. The state A has 1600 bits (25 lanes of 64 bits) and starts as all zeros; the rate r = {{rateBits}} bits ({{rateLanes}} lanes) takes the input, the capacity c = {{capacityBits}} bits stays hidden. This lab is a teaching tool: never type a real key into it.
plugin.kmac.step.encodeKey: Encode the key (SP 800-185 §4.3, step 1): encode_string(K) puts the key length in bits in front of K, left_encode({{keyBits}}) = {{lengthEncoded}}, then the {{keyBytes}} key bytes follow. bytepad(…, {{rateBytes}}) adds left_encode({{rateBytes}}) = {{rateEncoded}} in front and fills up with zeros to {{encodedBytes}} bytes = {{blocks}} × r. The key thus fills whole rate blocks of its own, and the message starts at a block boundary.
plugin.kmac.step.encodeLength: Encode the output length (SP 800-185 §4.3, step 2): right_encode(L) for L = {{bits}} bits ({{bytes}} bytes) is {{encoded}}, the value followed by its byte count. It comes after the message, so the requested length is part of the input: a KMAC tag of another length is an unrelated value, not a prefix of this one.
plugin.kmac.step.encodeLengthXof: Encode the output length (SP 800-185 §4.3.1): KMACXOF appends right_encode(0) = {{encoded}} instead of L. The input does not fix the length, so a longer output starts with the shorter one.
plugin.kmac.step.pad: Padding (SP 800-185 §3.3, §4.3): KMAC is cSHAKE with the function name N = “{{functionName}}” and the customization string S = “{{customization}}”. First comes the {{prefixBytes}}-byte prefix bytepad(encode_string(N) ‖ encode_string(S), r), then the {{newXBytes}}-byte input (encoded key ‖ {{bytes}} message bytes ‖ encoded length), the cSHAKE domain bits 00 and pad10*1. As bytes the padding is {{tail}}. The padded input has {{paddedBytes}} bytes = {{blocks}} × r ({{rateBytes}} bytes).
plugin.kmac.step.padNoS: Padding (SP 800-185 §3.3, §4.3): KMAC is cSHAKE with the function name N = “{{functionName}}” and here an empty customization string S. Because N is not empty, cSHAKE still adds its prefix: first come the {{prefixBytes}} bytes bytepad(encode_string(N) ‖ encode_string(S), r), then the {{newXBytes}}-byte input (encoded key ‖ {{bytes}} message bytes ‖ encoded length), the cSHAKE domain bits 00 and pad10*1. As bytes the padding is {{tail}}. The padded input has {{paddedBytes}} bytes = {{blocks}} × r ({{rateBytes}} bytes).
plugin.kmac.step.absorb: Absorb block {{n}}: its {{rateBytes}} bytes, read as {{rateLanes}} little-endian lanes, are XORed into the first {{rateLanes}} lanes of A (the rate). The {{capacityLanes}} capacity lanes stay untouched. Lane A[0,0] is now {{lane0}}.
plugin.kmac.step.theta: θ, round {{round}}: C[x] is the XOR of the five lanes of column x, and D[x] = C[x−1] ⊕ ROT(C[x+1], 1). Every lane A[x,y] is XORed with D[x], so each bit now depends on 11 bits of the old state. Here C[0] = {{c0}} and D[0] = {{d0}}.
plugin.kmac.step.rho: ρ, round {{round}}: every lane is rotated left by its own fixed offset (FIPS 202 Table 2), e.g. A[1,0] by 1 bit and A[0,1] by 36 bits; A[0,0] stays. The 25 offsets are all different mod 64, so bits move between the slices.
plugin.kmac.step.pi: π, round {{round}}: the lanes change places, A′[x,y] = A[(x + 3y) mod 5, x]. Only A[0,0] stays where it is. Together with ρ, this spreads neighbouring bits across the whole state.
plugin.kmac.step.chi: χ, round {{round}}: each lane is combined with the next two in its row, A′[x,y] = A[x,y] ⊕ (¬A[x+1,y] ∧ A[x+2,y]). The AND makes χ the only non-linear step mapping (degree 2).
plugin.kmac.step.iota: ι, round {{round}}: lane A[0,0] is XORed with the round constant RC = {{rc}}, giving {{lane0}}. Without ι, all 24 rounds would be identical and the permutation would keep symmetries.
plugin.kmac.step.round: Round {{round}}: θ, ρ, π, χ and ι in one step (RC = {{rc}}). Lane A[0,0] is now {{lane0}}.
plugin.kmac.step.permute: Keccak-f[1600] number {{n}}: all {{rounds}} rounds of θ, ρ, π, χ and ι in one step. Lane A[0,0] is now {{lane0}}.
plugin.kmac.step.squeeze: Squeeze {{n}}: the {{rateBytes}} rate bytes of the state are read out. Output bytes {{from}} … {{to}} take the first {{taken}} of them. If more output is needed, Keccak-f[1600] runs again first.
plugin.kmac.error.keyLength: The key has {{length}} bytes; at most 64 are allowed.
plugin.kmac.error.inputLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; at most 200 are allowed.
plugin.kmac.error.customizationLength: The customization string S has {{length}} bytes; at most 64 are allowed.
plugin.kmac.error.encoding: Unknown input format “{{encoding}}”: choose text or hex.
